method: Exhaustive raw byte-for-byte diff of the two firmware images (research/firmware/originals/firmware_autopilot868.bin vs firmware_autopilot915.bin, both 70768 bytes), cross-checked against the existing census `diff` subcommand (tools/census/aptrace_census.py diff autopilot868 autopilot915 --json), which independently compares function fingerprints/hashes, MMIO sites, pin configs, hardware registers, and string constants. No new Ghidra analysis, no Unicorn, no SMT was run; both firmware images were already fully built/reduced in the census database prior to this audit.

raw_byte_diff.note: Every byte in both 70768-byte images is identical except this single 4-byte range. This is an exhaustive, complete result (every byte was compared), not a sample.

value_autopilot868.interpretation: 864,000,000 Hz (864 MHz) -- radio center frequency, EU/868MHz-band variant

value_autopilot915.interpretation: 915,000,000 Hz (915 MHz) -- radio center frequency, US/other 915MHz-band variant

actual_differences.provenance: Copied from flash to RAM 0x20000000 by Reset_Handler__ADAFRUIT_CORE's generic .data copy loop (xref at flash 0x0000cc62, READ of flash 0x14c40). RAM 0x20000000 is READ by radio_bringup__THIRD_PARTY (0x0000610c, xref at 0x6114) -- the same already-established radio chip-ID-probe/post-probe-config function characterized in docs/replacement/autopilot-gap-audit.md's Gap Resolution B (radio transport).
evidence: docs/replacement/autopilot-gap-audit.md (radio transport / Gap Resolution B, radio_bringup__THIRD_PARTY already characterized)
actual_differences.replacement_contract_relevance: None -- lies entirely within the RF-band configuration boundary (radio center frequency), not MCU-side protocol/motor/persistence/trigger semantics. Confirms hardware-reference.md's already-documented '868/915 variants differ only in radio configuration' claim, now exhaustively proven for AutoPilot (previously only proven for Mando).

mechanical_artifacts_not_counted_as_diff.description: tools/census/aptrace_census.py diff's 'residual_priority_diffs' list: 48 residual functions where autopilot868 and autopilot915 report a different mechanical residual_priority score and/or a different function name. Every one of these 48 entries has entry_a == entry_b (same address in both images) AND an identical exact_hash (i.e. byte-for-byte identical function bodies, independently confirmed by this audit's own raw file diff, which found zero differing bytes anywhere in the executable code region). The priority-score differences stem from unequal dynamic-coverage ingestion (autopilot868: 19 ingested runs across 6 scenarios; autopilot915: 1 ingested run across 1 scenario -- residual_priority.py's scoring includes a dynamic-coverage-proximity signal). The 13 name differences (e.g. 'tc0_isr_completion__CUSTOM' on 868 vs 'FUN_00005be8' on 915) reflect that this session's semantic-classification passes (1-9) and Gap Resolution A/B were run against autopilot868 only -- autopilot915 has not yet been semantically classified at all, per this task's own baseline framing.
mechanical_artifacts_not_counted_as_diff.note: Not a firmware behavior difference of any kind -- an artifact of unequal analysis progress on the two images, not of unequal code. No inspection performed (correctly out of scope: 'Do not re-classify AutoPilot915 function-by-function').

replacement_contract_matrix_basis: Every one of these 21 subsystems lives entirely in code/data outside the single 4-byte differing range (DIFF-1, an RF center-frequency constant consumed only by the radio-bringup routine). Since the raw byte diff exhaustively found zero other differences anywhere in either 70768-byte image, every function implementing any of these subsystems is proven byte-identical between autopilot868 and autopilot915 -- not inferred from partial sampling.
pass_b_note: No items were classified POTENTIAL_BEHAVIOR_CHANGE or UNRESOLVED, so Pass B (bounded inspection) was not entered.

conclusion.summary: The AutoPilot868 replacement behavioral contract (docs/replacement/autopilot-gap-audit.md, research/generated/autopilot-replacement-gaps.json) can be used unchanged for AutoPilot915, with exactly one addendum: the radio center-frequency constant (864 MHz vs 915 MHz) that a replacement's own radio-bringup code must set per build, mirroring the vendor firmware's own single .data-constant difference.
